memory_update.text: Add SABR as the US-listed reference rail for travel distribution middleware, but mark leverage/restructuring and NDC disintermediation as key later-layer risks.
Add WEX to the underfollowed lane as a virtual-card and B2B supplier-payment infrastructure candidate for OTAs and travel intermediaries.
Add RSKD to the underfollowed lane as a small-cap travel fraud/chargeback candidate due to the 2026 Outpayce/Amadeus airline-payments integration.
Add AGYS as an underfollowed property-connectivity and hotel-operations software candidate; verify whether PMS/POS integrations create durable distribution/payment/loyalty chokepoint exposure.

Several highly relevant hotel-connectivity names appear non-US-listed or private, including SiteMinder, RateGain/DHISCO, Shiji, Cloudbeds, Mews, Travelport, and Outpayce/Amadeus. Later passes should decide whether non-US listings are allowed or retained only as context anchors.

node: Travel distribution middleware, property connectivity, payments routing, loyalty infrastructure, and fraud prevention
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the travel distribution/payments/fraud infrastructure node with a two-lane funnel. Sabre is retained as the core reference rail for GDS/distribution context, while WEX, Riskified, and Agilysys form the underfollowed discovery lane across virtual-card supplier payments, airline/travel fraud screening, and hotel property/POS operating systems. The key bottleneck hypothesis remains plausible but uneven: direct GDS exposure is concentrated, while second-order exposure may be hidden in payment authorization, chargeback guarantees, virtual cards, PMS/POS integrations, and hospitality workflow software. No investment recommendation is made.
